subject: Procurement questionnaire: telemetry access, SLO measurement, and temporary exception process
messages:

Subject: SLO measurement, monitoring and dashboard access — procurement questionnaire

Hi Neha,

Thanks for taking our RFP packet last week. To move procurement forward we need written answers to the telemetry / SLO section — the security team is particularly focused on how you measure availability and latency, and what access customers get to the measurement data. Could you confirm the following items for us?

1) Exact SLO definitions you measure (availability/uptime: definition, measurement window)
2) Latency metrics reported (p50/p95/p99), what endpoint these apply to, and how you aggregate (per-minute sliding window, etc.)
3) Sampling / data retention (raw samples, aggregation retention periods)
4) Alerting: on-call coverage, thresholds that trigger PagerDuty/ops escalation, and SLA credit triggers
5) Customer access: read-only dashboard options, API endpoints for metrics, export formats
6) Exception handling: process and timeline for temporary SLO exceptions during onboarding or migrations

If you have a short SLO spec doc and a read-only dashboard invite we can attach those to our procurement binder. Prefer to get answers by EOD Thursday PT so our legal team can draft the amendment.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Ruiz | Sr. Procurement Manager
StormPort Analytics

Subject: Re: SLO measurement, monitoring and dashboard access — procurement questionnaire

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. See answers inline below and attached a compact SLO/telemetry spec we maintain for procurement reviewers. Ben is cc'ed for the technical details and the Grafana invite.

1) SLO definitions:
   - Availability ("API availability"): percentage of 5xx-free production requests to the public inference API over a rolling 30-day window. We use a 1-minute bucket to compute availability; an interval is counted as failed if >=1 server-side 5xx in that minute. Target: 99.9% (standard), 99.95% for enterprise Dedicated plans.

2) Latency metrics:
   - Reported per-route: p50, p95, p99 on end-to-end request latency (client request arrival to final token emitted). Aggregation: 5-minute sliding windows rolled up to hourly/daily for dashboards. We report both per-request and token-level breakdowns in the spec.

3) Sampling / retention:
   - Raw request samples retained for 90 days (production logs). Aggregated hourly metrics retained for 13 months. Raw payloads are redacted by default (no customer prompt content stored in telemetry unless explicitly enabled).

4) Alerting / escalation:
   - Alerts configured at p98 latency breach and availability drop >0.25 percentage points vs rolling baseline for 3 consecutive 5-minute buckets. PagerDuty coverage 24/7 for Severity 1; on-call escalation policy is in our runbook. SLA credit calculations kick in when availability falls below contractual threshold for the full measurement window; credits are calculated per the SLA section in the contract.

5) Customer access:
   - Read-only Grafana dashboards (Grafana Cloud / Grafana Enterprise) + an API for metric export (Prometheus-compatible endpoint). We can provide dashboard invites (read-only) and short-lived API tokens. Exports available in Prometheus text format or CSV.

6) Exception handling:
   - Temporary exception (eg, during migration) can be requested via a formal "SLO Exception Request" (template attached). Typical approval path: Product Ops -> Reliability Lead -> Legal (if credits or contractual terms change). Temporary exceptions are usually limited to 30 days; longer or permanent changes require contract amendment and executive approval.

Attachments: redwood-slo-metrics-spec.pdf (compact spec), temporary-exception-form.pdf (request template)

If this looks good I can have Ben send the Grafana invite and provide the dashboard view that maps each metric to contract language. Happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow.

Best,

Raj / Elena — thanks for the questions; below are more precise technical answers and pointers. Quoting the spec where helpful.

- Raw logs: we retain request-level metadata (timestamp, request_id, route, response_code, processing_time). Raw request/response bodies are redacted by default; customers can opt into extended telemetry for debugging with explicit consent and contract language. Logs are stored in an append-only object store with immutable versions and SHA256 checksums; audit logs capture admin access and changes.

- Prometheus endpoint security: we support both mTLS and IP allowlist for scrape access. For customers that cannot use mTLS we can provide a read-only Grafana Cloud account tied to their corporate SSO. The metrics endpoint exposes only aggregated metrics (counters/gauges/histograms) and never raw prompt text.

- Exception approvals and data controls: temporary SLO exceptions do not change data retention defaults. Any exception that requests retention or access changes must be separately approved by Security and Legal and logged in the exception record. Our exception template requires a rationale, start/end dates, impacted metrics, and compensating controls.

- Measurement details (from spec): availability computed as (1 - failed_minutes/total_minutes) over 30-day rolling window; failed_minutes are 1-minute buckets with any server-side 5xx. Latency p99 computed over successful requests in the same window; we use HDR histograms to compute percentiles.

- Dashboard access: I just sent a read-only Grafana invite ("Grafana: StormPort - Redwood (read-only)") to elena@stormport.com. If you'd prefer API pulls we can issue a scoped Prometheus scrape token valid for 24 hours (or longer via contract).

Attachments: grafana-readonly-invite.url (invite), temporary-exception-form.pdf (filled with example).

If you want, I can attach a one-page runbook excerpt showing the on-call flow and threshold definitions. Would a 30-min technical sync on Monday work?
